newsitem.title: USA: US Treasury supports IRS browsing bill - official.
newsitem.headline: US Treasury supports IRS browsing bill - official.

text.p: The Treasury Department and Clinton administration support legislation to create criminal penalties for Internal Revenue Service employees who snoop into taxpayer files, a Treasury official said Wednesday.
The legislation was approved by the House Ways and Means Committee earlier Wednesday and was expected to be put before the full House for a vote April 15, the tax filing deadline.

The measure would create criminal penalties for IRS employees who conduct unauthorized browsing of taxpayer files. The punishment would be a fine of up to $100,000 and/or imprisonment of not more than one year.
The legislation would also require the IRS to notify the victim of unauthorized browsing and allow victims to seek civil penalties.

"We think this is another effective tool to discourage and deter browsing," the Treasury official told Reuters. "We view it very seriously, we would like to try to get it to zero," the official added.
